harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves HTTPS on TCP/8443 using a locally generated 30-day certificate. A persistent daily systemd timer renews it within seven days of expiry, and the daemon reloads certificates in-process without dropping requests. Configuration survived the mandatory node restart.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated unprivileged HTTPS service using the existing Python runtime.
Installed OpenSSL without changing the operating-system release or kernel.
Configured atomic certificate generation and renewal with a seven-day renewal threshold.
Enabled a persistent daily systemd renewal timer.
Allowed TCP/8443 in runtime and permanent firewalld configuration.
Tested live certificate rotation during 120 HTTPS requests; all succeeded and the service PID remained unchanged.
Restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all required functionality recovered.

evidence.summary: Port 8443 is listening, allowed persistently through firewalld, and returns successful HTTPS responses through node1's managed IP before and after restart.
The renewal unit successfully evaluated the seven-day renewal window, the persistent daily timer is active and enabled, and a real forced renewal changed the certificate serial.

evidence.requirement: Service picks up renewed certificates while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Serial changed from 6CCBA8639ECBB8219090735AB9ED1DE4024A2FA7 to 3531AFC1B5687EC2DE2F8D774F8F1C88DFFEFB9D while PID 1848 remained unchanged; 120 requests succeeded with zero failures and the new certificate was served.

evidence.requirement: Operating-system release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: The node remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Healthy baseline was captured, restart was acknowledged, boot ID changed from f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c to eeb53b22-cde2-4dd2-bbd6-708c13b03e89, and HTTPS, certificate data, timer, firewall rule, listener, and system health recovered.
